title: Rookies Worth a Look
markdown:
<sub>Proposed by the synthesis, not on the user's list.</sub>

**Summary.** Only three rookies have a clear path to real minutes and usage this season: Cameron Boozer, Caleb Wilson and Yaxel Lendeborg. The high-pick guards and AJ Dybantsa belong in the 1 USD flyer zone, and you should expect rookie guards to hurt FG% and turnovers early. Leave every other rookie on waivers and add one only if a specific injury or role change happens.

## Most rookie classes give only a few useful players

The experts expect little from rookies. At best, a class gives one top 50 player and three top 100 players. Another expert says most classes give only three or four relevant players. Drafters still take far too many rookies near the end of drafts. Our league drafts 144 players, so plan on about three or four rookies being worth real auction money, not eight or ten. ([06-25](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=315), [09-03](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=837))

Judge a rookie by his situation, minutes, usage and non-scoring stats. Do not judge him by where he was picked in the NBA draft. This class shows why. The No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa is a 1 USD player for us. The No. 5 and No. 6 picks, Keaton Wagler and Mikel Brown Jr., sit at or below the edge of our pool. Yaxel Lendeborg is a 24-year-old rookie, and he has a clearer path because he is projected to start. ([09-03](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1315), [AJ Dybantsa](#player/155), [Keaton Wagler](#player/576), [Mikel Brown Jr.](#player/70), [Yaxel Lendeborg](#player/330))

## The three with a real path

Cameron Boozer is the top rookie. He was the No. 3 pick and is the projected starter in Memphis. His value comes late. The experts rank him outside the top 70 early and at a top 25 to 35 level by our playoffs. Memphis also plays 4, 4 and 4 games in weeks 19 to 21. Pay 10 to 15 USD. Above that, you are paying for preseason buzz. He fits punt TO builds and may fit punt 3PM builds. Do not sell him after a slow start, because the case for him is about March. Early on, check his minutes in Iisalo's short-stint rotation and how many threes he takes. ([Cameron Boozer](#player/52))

Caleb Wilson was the No. 4 pick and is a projected starter in Chicago. Experts take him around picks 86 to 89, which makes him a mid-to-late auction target in the 4 to 6 USD range. His rebounds, blocks and steals help teams that need frontcourt defensive stats. His 74.7% FT and low assists hurt least in builds that already give those up. Check whether the Bulls keep feeding him usage under Splitter, how many threes he takes, and whether his efficiency settles. ([Caleb Wilson](#player/613))

Yaxel Lendeborg is the cheap one. Experts take him around picks 98 to 106 as a starter, but the market prices him near the end of the draft, so 1 or 2 USD can land him. He gives a little of everything, with blocks as his best category, and he is a natural punt 3PM fit. Check that he keeps the starting job under Kerr. Plan to sell or replace him before Butler and Moody return. If you sell him in a trade, do it before the 2027-03-04 deadline. ([Yaxel Lendeborg](#player/330))

## Rookie guards: expect poor shooting

Rookie point guards are almost always bad for fantasy because of efficiency problems. Be skeptical of drafting them. FG% in our league is a team ratio, so a guard taking about 14 shots a night moves it more than a low-volume bench player does. Draft a rookie guard only if your build can absorb an FG% and TO hit, or if your bigs shoot well enough to cover for him. ([10-04](https://youtu.be/tnzmsYUA4yQ?t=1413))

Darryn Peterson projects at 45.2% FG on about 14.5 shots with 2.1 turnovers. Darius Acuff Jr. projects at 42.6% FG on about 14 shots with 2.5 turnovers. Both bring points, and Peterson adds steals while Acuff adds assists. Cap Peterson at 1 to 3 USD and Acuff at 1 to 2 USD. For Peterson, check whether he starts and whether his FG% and turnovers get better. For Acuff, check whether his FG% stays above 40% and whether his preseason usage holds next to LaVine and Sabonis. ([10-04](https://youtu.be/tnzmsYUA4yQ?t=1413), [Darryn Peterson](#player/438), [Darius Acuff Jr.](#player/2))

Mikel Brown Jr. projects at 41.6% FG with about 2 turnovers, and nobody knows yet when he will be available. He is a 1 USD final pick at most and more likely a waiver target, with his value in the second half. Keaton Wagler is a backup point guard with likely efficiency problems. Skip him in the auction. ([10-04](https://youtu.be/tnzmsYUA4yQ?t=1413), [Mikel Brown Jr.](#player/70), [Keaton Wagler](#player/576))

## The 1 USD flyer zone and the two-week rule

Uncertain rookies belong in the flyer zone. In a 12-team league that is around picks 120 to 130, the end of the active roster or the start of the bench. In our auction, that means your last one or two roster spots at 1 or 2 USD. Use no more than one or two of those spots on rookies. Most classes give only a few relevant players. ([06-25](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=867), [09-03](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=837))

AJ Dybantsa is the clearest example. Every expert says to avoid him in the top 100 for category leagues. He sits behind Trae Young and Anthony Davis and may play only about 28 minutes early. Only his points stand out, and his turnovers make him a fit only for punt TO builds. Take him at 1 USD and let someone else pay 4 to 6 USD. Morez Johnson Jr. is also a 1 USD flyer at most, and only for a big-man build. Aday Mara's rising preseason ADP comes from hype, not from a regular-season role, so never pay more than 1 USD for him. ([06-25](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=867), [AJ Dybantsa](#player/155), [Morez Johnson Jr.](#player/286), [Aday Mara](#player/349))

Use Summer League and preseason to set these prices. If a rookie is named a starter before 2026-10-18, push him higher. That would apply to Hannes Steinbach if Charlotte names him the starter. If a flyer does nothing in the first two weeks of the season, drop him. You can pick him up again later. With daily FAB and up to 6 adds per week, a 1 USD rookie costs you little to cut. ([06-25](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=1204), [Hannes Steinbach](#player/532))

## Waiver watch: rookies waiting for an opening

Rookies who could help in blocks or steals if they win minutes: Hannes Steinbach (if he takes the Charlotte center job), Ugonna Onyenso (if Duren or Reed get hurt), Rafael Castro (if Kessler gets hurt), Trevon Brazile (if he wins backup power forward behind Aaron Gordon) and Morez Johnson Jr. (if Gafford is traded). Onyenso is on a two-way deal. Two-way players can still be worth rostering late in the season when they play. ([07-23](https://youtu.be/LUTYUdXBG1M?t=1327), [Hannes Steinbach](#player/532), [Ugonna Onyenso](#player/428), [Rafael Castro](#player/730), [Trevon Brazile](#player/60), [Morez Johnson Jr.](#player/286))

Guards who need an injury ahead of them: Kingston Flemings (CJ McCollum), Sergio de Larrea (Kyrie Irving, plus 16 Dallas back-to-backs), Ryan Conwell (Dru Smith out), Meleek Thomas (Harden or Mitchell), Christian Anderson (Coby White's calf) and Emanuel Sharp (Malik Monk). Treat any of them as a short-term streamer, not a hold. The guard shooting warning still applies, so check their FG% before you add them. ([10-04](https://youtu.be/tnzmsYUA4yQ?t=1413), [Kingston Flemings](#player/177), [Sergio de Larrea](#player/132), [Ryan Conwell](#player/115), [Meleek Thomas](#player/546), [Christian Anderson](#player/17), [Emanuel Sharp](#player/508))

Rookies who could get a late youth push near our playoffs: Brayden Burries and Mikel Brown Jr. Check their minutes from February on. Some rookies offer little even with minutes: Isaiah Evans gives only threes, Braden Smith gives only assists, and Alex Karaban, Karim Lopez and Labaron Philon have no category strength. Check them only if a major injury forces them into the rotation. ([Brayden Burries](#player/77), [Mikel Brown Jr.](#player/70), [Isaiah Evans](#player/169), [Braden Smith](#player/521), [Alex Karaban](#player/303), [Karim Lopez](#player/339), [Labaron Philon](#player/441))

## Where the sources split

The sources disagree on several of the rookies who matter. On Caleb Wilson, ESPN is high and Yahoo is lower. The experts sit near Yahoo at picks 86 to 89 and say not to chase him at ESPN's level. On threes, Yahoo projects 1.3 per game for both Boozer and Lendeborg, while ESPN projects 0.3. If ESPN is right, both are cleaner punt 3PM fits. If Yahoo is right, they help in more categories. On Lendeborg and Mara, expert or preseason ADP is far above the site ranks. Experts back Lendeborg because he is projected to start, while Mara's ADP rests on hype. Check the first week of box scores before you trust either side. ([Caleb Wilson](#player/613), [Cameron Boozer](#player/52), [Yaxel Lendeborg](#player/330), [Aday Mara](#player/349))

- Jayden Quaintance: The newest note says he may not play at all this season after another knee surgery.
- Javon Small: He is not a rookie. He is a two-way player with a previous NBA season, so he does not fit a rookie article.
- Jalen Slawson: He is not a rookie. He is a two-way player who played 13 games last season, so he does not fit a rookie article.
